title: Schedule F: Trump Purges 50,000 Deep State Civil Servants as Political Enemies
description_short: Schedule F: Trump Purges 50,000 Deep State Civil Servants as Political Enemies
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an order restoring a policy that reclassifies some career federal positions as Schedule Policy/Career. The Office of Personnel Management says covered jobs involve policy-influencing work and lose standard removal procedures while retaining merit-based hiring. The order changes employment protections; the supplied record does not establish that 50,000 workers were purged.
description_long: On his first day in office, January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order reinstating and renaming Schedule F — a policy that strips civil service job protections from approximately 50,000 federal employees, reclassifying them as at-will workers who can be fired without cause. The order was engineered by Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and OMB Director Russ Vought, both of whom had long championed the strategy during Trump's first term. Trump and his allies framed the entire career federal workforce as a conspiratorial deep state populated by enemies within who had sabotaged his first administration — rhetoric rejected by legal experts and historians as fabricated justification for a power grab unprecedented in modern presidencies. In parallel, Elon Musk's DOGE team conducted mass layoffs across dozens of agencies, with senior DOJ officials, Coast Guard commandants, and State Department diplomats dismissed within hours of the inauguration. The American Federation of Government Employees and AFSCME filed lawsuits in February 2025 alleging unconstitutional authority, with AFSCME President Lee Saunders stating Schedule F is a shameless attempt to politicize the federal workforce by replacing thousands of dedicated, qualified civil servants with political cronies. Critics noted the irony that Trump branded career civil servants enemies based purely on the conspiracy theory that loyalty to law rather than loyalty to Trump constitutes treason.
notes: Reason: OPM confirms reclassification of some policy-influencing positions, but not a completed purge of 50,000 employees or selection of workers as political enemies.
Proposed correction: “Trump Restores Schedule F Classification for Policy-Influencing Federal Jobs.”
